newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB hits 11-month low, SocGen negative.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB hits 11-month low, SocGen negative.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc slid to an 11-month low on Friday amid continued fears over its lucrative soccer broadcasting rights, dealers and analysts said.
Analysts at SocGen were said to have rated the stock a "sell" and to have set a target of 400p, though analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment.

With some fund managers said to be clearing the underperforming stock out of their portfolios at the end of the first half, BSkyB was down 2p at 453-1/2 by 1051 GMT. Earlier it hit a day's low of 443p, its lowest since July, 1996.

A report in the Evening Standard on Thursday said the English Premier League was seeking more money from BSkyB for television rights next year, when Sky channels will be broadcast through a planned digital television service.
Reports earlier this week had raised concerns that the Premiership was considering setting up its own service when the current contract expires in 2001.
BSkyB shares have been under severe pressure since June 17 when the group said its chief executive Sam Chisholm would step down.

"It was always a 'blue-sky' (speculative) stock, it just looks as if people have given up on the dream and are starting to look more closely at what they are getting for their money," said one dealer.
"And fund managers don't want to be seen holding it when they present to their trustees."
Carlo Campomagnani, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said the current weakness of the shares reflected uncertainty about prospects for the company's soccer services.
"The stock has an incredible degree of volatility and with recent reports we are dealing with issues that will probably not become clear for a while," Campomagnani said.
Yet some said the recent steep decline had taken BSkyB shares to a level where they looked attractive.
"Of course we must at some point get to a level where there is value," said another analyst, who asked not to be named. He said 450p looked to be a "fair value" level for the shares.
"Sky is still the leading provider of pay-TV in the country and I would not underestimate the value of distribution," the analyst said.
